headline: Brent Crude Rises Above $90 After US Strikes on Iran and Escalation in the Strait of Hormuz
summary: International crude jumped more than 5.6% to $90.99 per barrel after Washington bombed military positions in Hormuz and the UAE intercepted an Iranian drone. Global alarm grew over energy supply.
why: Brent is the main international crude benchmark, and Gulf shipping through the Strait of Hormuz carries a large share of seaborne oil. Supply disruption there quickly feeds into global fuel and energy prices.

source.name: Diario Río Negro | Periodismo en la Patagonia

sources.name: Diario Río Negro | Periodismo en la Patagonia

why_moved: Attacks and interceptions in the Gulf raised fears of disruption to oil shipments through Hormuz, and Brent jumped more than 5.6% in the report.
